main_body: A flat snow-and-dark-ground terrain patch (pale blue-white snow blobs over dark green-grey mottled ground), tiled 4x3; no standing volume.
top_band: none (terrain tile, no standing object; a flat ground texture)
evidence: Terrain ground patch viewed from above, not a standing object. There is no top/front structure to judge, and no receding side faces are drawn. The terrain kind is plausible, so the 3/4 contract is not applicable and nothing violates it.

style.evidence: The patch uses about 5 lightness steps across snow (white, pale blue, blue-grey) and dark ground (grey-green, dark green-grey), with speckle dots in the dark areas and a few bright white pixel sparkles. The snow lobes are mostly smooth flat pale areas, some about 5x5 or larger, with little grain. The pattern is also a very regular repeat of identical blobs, so it reads as stamped and mechanical next to the Beodeul grass and paving, which vary more tile to tile. No outlines are used, which is fine for ground. Overall it is a bit thinner and flatter than the reference, mainly because of the plain snow areas and the rigid repetition.
